liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Row Jimmy** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds it remarkably crisp; Crowd roars around 2:40 during Jerry's first solo [26][31]
- **Picasso Moon** (1 review): Reviewer says the ending is a trainwreck, explaining why it was left off Dozin' [35]
- **Blow Away** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the best ever; Brent had the crowd during his rap [31]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer names the China Cat into Rider pairing an all-time favorite; set two took off after Victim [28]
- **Dear Mr. Fantasy** (1 review): Reviewer found it unusually weak, followed by a pretty hot Gimme Some Lovin' [36]

## Setlist highlights

- **wait-a-minute rap**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [37]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-03-26.135063.bltz.flac2496** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 155 min [1]
- **gd1990-03-26.sennME80.wklitz.94411.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 152 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [7]. Said about its sound: Recording has clear vocals and instrument separation; audience audible and Brent is audible when not playing lead, unlike the pre-FM [31]
- **gd1990-03-26.149395.FOB.Schoeps.Mattes.Miller.Noel.reMaster.t-flac1648**: source not stated; 20 songs; 155 min [10]
- **gd1990-03-26.142991.FOB.Schoeps.Mattes.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: source not stated; 20 songs; 155 min [11]
- **gd1990-03-26.sbd.griesman.6697.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 140 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [14]
- **gd90-03-26.sbd.gorinsky.8508.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 139 min; rated 4.43/5 by 7 [15]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the arena crowd's energy was high and the first set felt exceptional for a late-era show [26]
- Arena management reportedly included Jerry in something on a wall; reviewer nearly cried during Brokedown Palace [28]
- Reviewer asks about the story behind a python at Jerry's feet during the show [30]
- Reviewer recalls Brent standing up during Blow Away [36]
- Reviewer recommends also getting the shows from the two preceding days, March 24 and 25 [32]
- Reviewer considers this the weakest show of the Albany run, though still good by spring 1990 standards [36]
- Big Railroad Blues was last played on 09-18-88 [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-03-26.135063.bltz.flac2496**: taped by Richard Berner friends; transferred by bltz; source: First set, Set II Victim, and, after China -> Rider: Richard Berner's B&K 4011's, 110 degrees ORTF, hand-held @ 5' high, Prolink -> Neumann Power Supply ->… [1]. Also: Master from an unreleased audience FOB DAT, part of the Original Master Rescue Project [1]
- **gd1990-03-26.sennME80.wklitz.94411.flac16**: taped by Keith Litzenberger; transferred by Keith Litzenberger; source: Sennheiser ME-80's>Technics SV-MD1 [7]
- **gd1990-03-26.149395.FOB.Schoeps.Mattes.Miller.Noel.reMaster.t-flac1648**: taped by Master Digital Audience Recording by Ted Mattes; transferred by Transfer by Charlie Miller Edited & reMastered using Adobe Audition by Joe Noel March 28, 2020; source: rom the Teddy Ballgame Archive - a reMaster of shnid 142991 Source: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4 MK21 (ORTF) > DAT (Panasonic SV-250) Location: Sec 5 Row E Seat 7 [10]
- **gd1990-03-26.142991.FOB.Schoeps.Mattes.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: flac16/48kHz ; Ted Mattes Master DAT Recording (FOB): Schoeps CMC4 MK21 (ORTF) > DAT (Panasonic SV-250); Location: Sec 5 Row E Seat 7; Charlie Miller [11]. Also: Recorded by Ted Mattes, transferred through Charlie Miller, with a patch source from Ray Ackerman [11]
- **gd1990-03-26.sbd.griesman.6697.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Randy Griesman; source: SBD>?>CD-r [14]. Also: Soundboard extracted and shortened by Randy Griesman on 12/23/2001; set one has dead air edited out [14]
- **gd90-03-26.sbd.gorinsky.8508.sbeok.shnf**: source: 24 track SBD MR>Healy 2 track Mixdown>C>DAT>CDR [15]. Also: Reviewer asks for an audience version, noting the soundboard circulating was what appeared on Dozin' [29]

Reviewer names the China Cat into Rider pairing an all-time favorite; set two took off after Victim

Reviewer asks for an audience version, noting the soundboard circulating was what appeared on Dozin'
Reviewer asks about the story behind a python at Jerry's feet during the show
Recording has clear vocals and instrument separation; audience audible and Brent is audible when not playing lead, unlike the pre-FM

Reviewer calls it the best ever; Brent had the crowd during his rap
Reviewer recommends also getting the shows from the two preceding days, March 24 and 25
Reviewer says the ending is a trainwreck, explaining why it was left off Dozin'

Reviewer considers this the weakest show of the Albany run, though still good by spring 1990 standards
